answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to stake a scarce, non-transferable credential minted only after prolonged, verifiable interaction on a shared terrace of mutual tasks. An agent that has cooperated for months under a sable reputation score earns a jade token that is burned on misbehavior. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real compute and time, because each must independently accumulate the same hard-earned history before it can act at scale.
